title: The footer shows settings, session and place on rows of their own, each filling the width
body:
Under the prompt sit the rule, the `context:` row and one status line. The status line holds the settings on the left and the session's numbers and state on the right, so on a narrow pane settings drop into `⋯` and numbers drop off. Nothing during a session shows which agent entry, folder, branch or session it is. Jack wants the prompt a little higher, and each footer row to fill the width with something at each edge, so the rows read with an even density.

## Proposal

From the top, below the rule:

```text
 context: 42%  ▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱
 auto   ·   opus   ·   effort high   ·   fast off   ·   ultracode off
 plan 2/5 · ↑128k ↓4.2k · .84                            decade · idle
 claude-coax · ~/projects/coax · dev          first daily drive of coax
```

- The settings row holds every setting chip, spread evenly across the width. When they do not fit at their normal spacing, the rest go into `⋯` as now.
- The session row holds the plan, tokens and cost on the left, and decade, the update notice and the working state on the right.
- A new place row holds the agent entry's name, the folder with the home folder shortened to `~`, and the git branch on the left, and the session's title on the right, cut with `…` when long. A part with nothing to show is left out.
- Colours as the status line has them now. On the place row the agent name is `accent`, the folder `blue` and the branch `green`, for Jack to react to.
